title: Duchy of Kalisz
capsule: The Duchy of Kalisz was a Piast appanage duchy in Greater Poland, carved from the fragmented Polish realm during the period of provincial division that followed the death of Mieszko III the Old. It existed as a recognizable distinct unit in the early thirteenth century, held briefly by Piast dukes as part of the complex web of partitioned Polish principalities before being reintegrated into the broader duchy of Greater Poland. The city of Kalisz itself was one of Poland's oldest trading centres, located on the amber route, and the duchy's brief independent existence reflects the wider pattern of succession crises and territorial partition that characterized the Polish lands between the death of Bolesław III Wrymouth (1138) and the reunification under Władysław I in 1320.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's attestation as a distinct territorial entity in the 1210–1220 window is inferred from charters and later chronicles; boundaries overlapped with adjacent Piast duchies and shifted repeatedly, making firm territorial delineation difficult.
